chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Fāris, who said:
A man wrote to him asking about the droppings of chickens: is salat (prayer) permissible in it? So he wrote: No.

The correct way to understand this narration is that salat (prayer) is not permissible in it when the chicken is jallāl; it is also possible that it is to be understood as a kind of recommendation, or as having been stated in taqiyyah, because that is the view of many of the ʿāmmah.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni populace or their juristic majority in this context
key_terms.جَلَّالًا: an animal that feeds on filth

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid if there is chicken droppings on one's clothing or body?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in relation to the droppings of chickens. The apparent prohibition is explained as applying when the chicken is jallāl, or alternatively as a recommendation or a ruling given in taqiyyah due to the view held by many of the ʿāmmah.
